classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the nonnegative square root as an absolute value, then transform a trigonometric graph on a restricted domain.

answer.short: $y=|\cos x|$ on $[0,2\pi]$. Zeros: $x=\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}$. Maximum value $1$ at $x=0,\pi,2\pi$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{\cos^2 x}\\y&=|\cos x|.\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=\cos x$ on $[0,2\pi]$ and reflect its negative portion across the $x$-axis. Keep sharp points at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi}{2}$.

spec.description: Absolute cosine over two pi, with closed endpoints, two sharp zeros and three maxima.
spec.mathematics: y=abs(cos(x)), 0<=x<=2*pi; zeros pi/2 and 3*pi/2; maxima 1 at 0, pi and 2*pi.
